solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: EP cut by Arctic Monkeys in rehearsal (8)

indicatorNotes.Monkeys: to monkey with something is to mess it about

annotation.surface: A record-label note: the band Arctic Monkeys cutting an EP while still in rehearsal.
annotation.walkthrough: The band name splits in two: 'Arctic' joins EP as fodder and 'Monkeys' is the verb. An EP is a short record.
annotation.definitionFit: Practice and rehearsal are both the run-through before the real thing.

entries.clue: Old man close to bar will get usual (3)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: one's old man is one's father

annotation.surface: Dad heading for the pub at closing time for his usual pint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Usual' reads as the regular drink, but it is the adjective: par is the normal level.
annotation.definitionFit: From golf and finance: par is the normal expected level, so an average result is described with it.

entries.clue: Track a box, perhaps, filled with indium (7)

indicatorNotes.filled with: the outer pieces are filled with the inner one

blocks.note: box is a kind of tree, hence 'perhaps'

annotation.surface: Tracking a delivery box that turns out to be full of a rare metal.
annotation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National; 'box' is the hedge shrub, not a container.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Merseyside racecourse famous for the Grand National is one of many horse-racing tracks.

entries.clue: Soldier in play collects military medal (5)

indicatorNotes.collects: the outer word gathers the other inside it

annotation.surface: An actor playing a soldier wins a medal for the role.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play' wants to be a stage play; it is the verb TOY. Tommy is the old nickname for a British private.
annotation.definitionFit: Tommy (from Tommy Atkins) is slang for a British soldier.

entries.clue: Red edges covered in blue, perhaps (7)

indicatorNotes.covered in: one piece is wrapped inside the other

blocks.note: blue is the Conservative colour, so a Tory

annotation.surface: Red borders painted over with blue, like a colour-mixing puzzle.
annotation.walkthrough: Blue here is political: it is the colour of Britain's Conservative party, and the 'Red' beside it plays on Labour.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this deep purplish shade, named from the kermes insect dye, is one kind of red.

entries.clue: State of abnormal insentience (4)

indicatorNotes.of: the answer is made of letters from the words that follow

annotation.surface: A doctor's phrase for a patient in an unusual state of unfeeling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' reads as condition, but it is a country: Mali in West Africa.
annotation.definitionFit: Mali is an independent state in West Africa.

entries.clue: Pencil in a compass you’ve picked up (7)

indicatorNotes.you’ve picked up: to pick something up is to hear it, so go by the sound

annotation.surface: Geometry class: pick up the pencil clipped into your compass.
annotation.walkthrough: Pencil and compass suggest drawing circles, but 'compass' is scope, and 'Pencil in' is to book provisionally.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: pencilling something in schedules it provisionally, as if it could be rubbed out, which is a way of setting it up.

entries.clue: I teach unit around about November for mock (11)

indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around N
indicatorNotes.about: the letters are turned about into a new order

annotation.surface: A teacher preparing a unit around November, in time for mock exams.
annotation.walkthrough: Mocks are British practice exams, which fits the teacher; here 'mock' is the adjective for fake.
annotation.definitionFit: As an adjective, mock means imitation or sham, as in mock Tudor, so not genuine.

entries.clue: Singer in Welsh service holding note (4)

indicatorNotes.holding: the service keeps the note inside it

annotation.surface: A Welsh choir singer at a chapel service holding a long note.
annotation.walkthrough: The singer is a bird, and the service is military, not a church one.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: singer often means a songbird, and this tiny brown bird has a famously loud song.

entries.clue: Very popular star I’m mean about (10)

annotation.surface: A hugely popular star admits to being stingy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mean' sits in the surface as stingy, but it is simply four letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Taste that follows the main current of opinion is the one most people share.

entries.clue: Bit of seafood ring scoffed by foolish person (7)

indicatorNotes.scoffed by: the eater swallows the other word

blocks.note: a sop is a weakling or softy
to ring is to call on the phone

annotation.surface: A calamari ring wolfed down by some fool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like calamari, but it is the phone verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this fan-shelled bivalve is one of the shellfish served in restaurants.

entries.clue: Where my butt might end up if horse bolts off path (6)

indicatorNotes.bolts: the horse runs off, leaving the word

blocks.clueFragment: Where my butt might end up
blocks.note: a cigarette butt is stubbed out there
horse is slang for heroin, H

annotation.surface: A rider picturing a nasty fall if the horse bolts off the trail.
annotation.walkthrough: The butt is a cigarette end, not a backside, and 'horse' is heroin, so the H leaves ASHTRAY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that has strayed has left its proper route.

entries.clue: Second company frogman picking up oyster finally in drink (11)

indicatorNotes.picking up: the frogman takes the letter inside
indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so only the end letter of 'oyster' is used

blocks.note: a crew is a company of workers

annotation.surface: A diver from a second team surfaces with an oyster from the drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is British slang for the sea, which suits the frogman; here it is a cocktail.
annotation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a vodka and orange juice drink.

entries.clue: Do nothing, say, to retain a good name (8)

indicatorNotes.retain: the outer word keeps the others within it

annotation.surface: Advice to keep quiet and do nothing if you want to protect your reputation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb STATE.
annotation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stay idle and make no progress.

entries.clue: European chaps bursting into number by Air (8)

indicatorNotes.bursting into: the chaps break into the song

blocks.note: an air is a tune, as is an aria

annotation.surface: Men bursting into a musical number on a flight, perhaps with Air France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as the song they sing; it only gives N, and the song is the capital-A Air.
annotation.definitionFit: Armenia is counted as a European nation, so an Armenian is a European.

entries.clue: People soon to take husband (7)

indicatorNotes.to take: the phrase takes in the letter

annotation.surface: Folk who will soon take a husband: brides-to-be.
annotation.walkthrough: 'People' looks like a noun but is the verb: to people a place is to fill it with inhabitants.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: settlers who people a land fill it and live there, which is what inhabiting means.

entries.clue: German tunes concertmaster’s radioed (6)

indicatorNotes.radioed: broadcast, so heard rather than seen

blocks.note: in Britain the concertmaster is called the leader of the orchestra

annotation.surface: German songs a concertmaster has broadcast on the radio.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. British orchestras call their first violin the leader, which is how concertmaster gives the sound.
annotation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, such as Schubert's.

entries.clue: Change one might spell using an S prefix (6)

indicatorNotes.prefix: a prefix is something attached to the front of a word, so the S goes before WITCH

annotation.surface: A spelling rule: change a word by sticking S on the front.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spell' pretends to be about letters, which the S backs up; it means casting spells.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to switch plans or sides is to change them.

entries.clue: Hit with police weapon deters a criminal (7)

indicatorNotes.criminal: the letters are crooked, so rearranged

annotation.surface: Zapping someone with a police stun gun stops a criminal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the noun at the end of the scene; it is the adjective telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Tasered means hit with a Taser, a police stun weapon.

entries.clue: Going through copy, submit material (8)

indicatorNotes.Going through: one word passes through the middle of the other

blocks.note: to posit is to put forward

annotation.surface: An editor going through copy before submitting the material.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' reads as newspaper copy but is the adjective meaning relevant, as in a material fact.
annotation.definitionFit: Material evidence is apposite, relevant to the matter.

entries.clue: Letters arriving out of the blue? (7)

annotation.definition: Letters arriving out of the blue?

blocks.note: not 'unexpectedly' but literally from the blue sky, by plane

annotation.surface: Letters that arrive unexpectedly, from nowhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of the blue' means unexpectedly, but read literally it is out of the sky, which is where airmail comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: Airmail is letters delivered by plane, down from the blue sky.

entries.clue: Material getting my boss frustrated? (7)

blocks.note: the setter's boss is the editor, ED

annotation.surface: Someone's work material leaving the boss exasperated.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter's boss is the newspaper editor. In British slang to be stuffed is to be thwarted or beaten, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Stuffed can mean thwarted, as in 'we got stuffed'.

entries.clue: Structural support or brass moulding on tap (8)

indicatorNotes.moulding: the letters are moulded into a new shape

annotation.surface: A plumber choosing a support or a brass fitting for a tap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brass moulding' looks like a metal fitting; 'moulding' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossbar is a horizontal bar that supports a structure.

entries.clue: Sausage eater apparently holding in a fat gut (6)

indicatorNotes.holding: the sausage eater holds the letter inside

blocks.note: Mr Punch, of the Punch and Judy puppet show, is famous for his string of sausages

annotation.surface: A sausage lover sucking in a fat belly.
annotation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a traditional British seaside puppet show in which Punch guards a string of sausages; 'apparently' flags the indirect reference.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a paunch is a pot belly, the gut grown fat.

entries.clue: Large earl bailing from jet, one caught in tailspin (5)

indicatorNotes.bailing from: the letters leave the jet, as a pilot bails out
indicatorNotes.caught in: the one is followed by c for caught

blocks.note: L and E are removed from PLANE, leaving PAN

annotation.surface: A large nobleman parachuting out of a jet that has gone into a spin.
annotation.walkthrough: The tailspin is the definition, not part of the crash: to be in a tailspin is to be in a panic.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative use: a plane in a tailspin is out of control, so the word came to mean a state of alarm.

entries.clue: Tax too much on small caravan (10)

blocks.note: on means over, as in a shelf over the fire
a caravan is a train of travellers or pack animals

annotation.surface: A complaint that caravan owners are overtaxed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tax' looks financial but means strain; the caravan is a camel train, not a holiday trailer.
annotation.definitionFit: Tax here means burden, as in 'taxing work', so to burden something beyond its limit is to overstrain it.

entries.clue: Judge issued a penalty in hearing (4)

indicatorNotes.in hearing: as heard, and a hearing is also a court sitting

annotation.surface: A judge handing out a fine at a court hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is the verb: a court finds a defendant guilty.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: a jury that returns a verdict for one side is deciding, or judging, the case that way.

entries.clue: The type that goes on horse (3)

blocks.note: to go on is to keep complaining at someone
an old or worn-out horse, in informal speech

annotation.surface: Someone who always talks about horses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goes on' also suggests a rider mounting, which is what makes the horse fit so neatly.
annotation.definitionFit: A nag is a person who keeps on at you, and an old horse.

entries.clue: During power outage, old maid becomes naughty (4)

indicatorNotes.outage: the power goes out of the word

annotation.surface: In a blackout, a prim spinster lets loose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'During' just places the scene; the power cut takes the P out of PRUDE.
annotation.definitionFit: Rude and naughty both describe risqué behaviour.

entries.clue: Billions with torment about privation and depression (5,3)

blocks.note: to dog is to plague or torment

annotation.surface: Billionaires tormented by thoughts of poverty and depression.
annotation.walkthrough: Churchill called his depression his black dog. 'About' is only 'concerning', not a reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: The black dog is a well-known name for depression.
